name: 2026-10-21-settleS1-gh200
status: DESCRIPTIVE: S1 measures; it certifies nothing and no model verdict is scored on its pages. The reading bands below choose the FORM v5 registers for F1, F2 and F3; they are not verdicts
design: DIAGNOSIS-A2 (moe-kernels-work 2026-10-21 diag-A2/DIAGNOSIS.md, offline, read-only over A2's tree at 36291487), section Q7's five measurements; the owner's decision of 2026-10-21: run S1 first so the sag (F1) and the re-reads (F3) are measured, not fitted, then design v5
tool: scripts/gh200_settleS1_session.sh (A2's pinned driver plus lines marked S1), scripts/dram_counter_route_s1.py (instrumentation only: ncu replay mode, cache control, metric list), scripts/power_proof_s1.py (S1-M0's load: torch.matmul, no kernel of ours), scripts/scoring/settleS1/read_s1.py (the reader)
seen: Every S1 page is SEEN for v5: any constant v5 takes from an S1 reading (A and tau per lock, the knee's form, a re-read refit) is SEEN-MEASURED or SEEN-FITTED, and no S1 page or E1-CAL page can test it. v5's blind test must use NEW shapes: rental B2's frozen pages (docs/registered/2026-10-20-tileB2-e1tile-gh200: JetMoE-8B, Phi-3.5-MoE and Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B, the shapes DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q6 names for each fix), never OLMoE-1B-7B, Mixtral 8x7B or Qwen2-57B-A14B, whose cells S1 and A2 measured

power_and_lock.rule: A2's (tileA2-gates P-W): the pre-setup dry run and the prelude refuse a card whose power.max_limit is under 900 W, no fallback to 700 W; the limit is set as A2 set it, nvidia-smi -pl 900 -sc 0 (scope 0 is the GPU's, 1 the module's, per nvidia-smi's documentation). S1 adds the read-back: the prelude polls (every 2 s, up to 30 s) until --query-gpu=enforced.power.limit (the power management algorithm's ceiling, the minimum of every limiter) and nvidia-smi -q -d POWER's GPU-scope Current Power Limit both read 900 W within 1 W, then writes power-set.txt; otherwise it REFUSES. A2 read 700 W from -q (Current and Requested) and 900 W from power.limit on every read of its session and never read enforced.power.limit, so the limit A2 ran under is not known (A2 publication)
power_and_lock.fallback: the owner's decision of 2026-10-21, pre-authorised: a read-back refusal at 900 W is recorded (s1-power.env S1_POWER_900=refused, power-set-unsettled-900.txt) and the SAME session sets nvidia-smi -pl 700 -sc 0 and repeats the read-back, requiring enforced.power.limit and the -q GPU-scope Current Power Limit both at 700 W; every unit then runs at 700 W (S1_POWER_W=700). A refusal at 700 W too stops the session. No other scope is tried (-sc 2 is not used)

outcomes.900 W read back: the owner's 900 W limit is in force as both readings say; M0 confirms it (ABOVE-700 possible) or shows a lower limiter (AT-700, CAP-BELOW-680)
outcomes.900 W refused, 700 W read back: the board behaves as A2's most likely did; S1's pages are at 700 W, comparable to A2's; the 900 W decision is recorded as not attainable on this board; M0 states whether 700 W held (AT-700) or another limiter is lower (CAP-BELOW-680); ABOVE-700 would mean the readings do not name the enforced limit
outcomes.both refused: the session stops before any page (about $1 of setup); no S1 reading exists

power_and_lock.lock_rule: every unit but M0 runs under nvidia-smi -lgc at the session lock 1410 MHz (the rung A2 held) with ncu --clock-control none, except S1-M2's pages at their own locks 1305 and 1005 MHz (and its same-board 1410 reference), and M0 (the power proof), which runs with no lock; the prelude locks, reads back and resets each unit lock once
power_and_lock.probe: no lock-hold probe: S1 certifies nothing and chooses no lock, and every page carries its own clock reading (sm__cycles_elapsed.avg over gpu__time_duration.sum per GEMM), so a lock that sags is the measurement itself, not a reason to move the session

M0.question: which GPU power limit holds: A2's -q readings (700 W) or its power.limit (900 W)? The limit every later S1 page runs under, and the likeliest source of the sag (DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q5: the SW power cap, 0x4, fired on A2's heavy pages at 1410)
M0.cells: no cells: torch.matmul 8192^3 bf16, back to back, 90 s, no clock lock (scripts/power_proof_s1.py)
M0.instrument: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,power.draw,enforced.power.limit,power.limit,clocks.sm,clocks.max.sm,clocks_event_reasons.active,temperature.gpu -lms 100 for the GEMM's length; -q -d POWER before and after
M0.unit: watts (GPU scope power.draw); seconds; share of samples
M0.quantity: busy samples (power.draw > 200 W); 1 s means (10 consecutive busy samples); the seconds of 1 s means over 720 W; the largest 1 s mean; the share of busy samples with the SW power cap bit 0x4; the busy clock's median against clocks.max.sm; enforced.power.limit as read

reading.ABOVE-700: 1 s means over 720 W cover >= 10 s
reading.AT-700: largest 1 s mean in [680, 720] W, SW power cap on >= half the busy samples, busy clock under max
reading.CAP-BELOW-680: SW power cap on >= half the busy samples and the largest 1 s mean under 680 W

constrains.session: ABOVE-700: a ceiling above 700 W held under S1's 900 W readings; S1's pages ran above A2's -q value. AT-700: a 700 W ceiling held although both read-backs said 900 W: the read-backs do not name the enforced limit on this platform, S1's pages ran at 700 W (as A2's most likely did) and the owner's 900 W decision was not in force. CAP-BELOW-680: another limiter (module or platform) holds below both; S1-M2's sag is read against it. UNDECIDED: no reading
constrains.F1: AT-700 or CAP-BELOW-680 with S1-M2 PRESENT: the sag is a power-cap transient at the enforced limit, so F1's A and tau are per limit as well as per lock and tile; ABOVE-700 with S1-M2 PRESENT: the sag persists with headroom, a kernel-start clock effect at the lock, not the cap

M1.question: DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q7 row 1: is the sag in the timed burst the one ncu's kernel replay shows (each kernel replayed in isolation after a cache flush and a save/restore)?
M1.cells: E1-CAL cells OLMoE 128x128 G 1 n 1 PT and n 4 PT, Qwen2-57B n 2 PT, NATIVE (copied cells, same shuffle seed: docs/registered/2026-10-21-settleS1-hist/olmoe-1b-7b-128g1-rp.json, qwen2-57b-a14b-128g1-rp.json)

instrument.kr: A2's byte-page instrument: ncu --replay-mode kernel --cache-control all --clock-control none under nvidia-smi -lgc 1410 (scripts/dram_counter_route_tile.py)
instrument.ar: ncu --replay-mode application --cache-control none, everything else the same (scripts/dram_counter_route_s1.py --s1-replay application)

M1.unit: microseconds per GEMM kernel launch (mean of the page's 3 measured calls); per cell, the call's w1 + w2
M1.quantity: off = gpu__time_duration.sum - sm__cycles_elapsed.avg / 1410 MHz per GEMM; d = off_app - off_kernel per GEMM and per cell

reading.INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENT: |median d_cell| <= 10 us and every |d_cell| <= 0.25 x off_kernel_cell + 5 us

constrains.F1: INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENT: the sag is not made by kernel replay's flush or save/restore; v5's F1 takes A and tau from counter pages (A2's, S1-M2's) as measured. INSTRUMENT-INFLATED: the kernel-replay A overstates the sag; v5's F1 takes its size from the application-replay offsets (per cell) and DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q1's clock/call split is re-read with them. INSTRUMENT-DEFLATED: the sag is larger in stream order; F1's A is taken from the application-replay pages, and the per-call timed residual (-32.3 us at 128) is compared with their per-cell sum. MIXED: no counter-page A enters v5 without a per-cell check against these three cells

M1.follow_up: in-burst per-GEMM CUDA events (a wrapper around pinned R3's timed path) are built only if M1 reads MIXED or INSTRUMENT-DEFLATED (owner, 2026-10-21)
M1.not_reproduced: application replay still serialises the profiled launches (ncu stops between them to read its counters), so the GEMMs are not as back to back as in R3's timed burst; the contrast isolates the flush and the save/restore, not the gaps

M2.question: DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q7 row 2: does the sag vanish at a lower lock (an apparatus fix), and where?
M2.cells: the OLMoE f128 counter page: 128x128x64 w8 s3, G 64, treads 1 to 9, NATIVE, SHARED and PRIVATE (54 GEMM cells)
M2.instrument: A2's byte-page instrument at the unit's own lock (1305, 1005, 1410 MHz)
M2.unit: microseconds per GEMM kernel; A in microseconds, tau in microseconds; f in MHz
M2.quantity: per lock L: off = t_ncu - cycles / L per GEMM cell; A(L), tau(L) of off = A (1 - exp(-t / tau)) (tau on a grid 50 to 4975 us, step 25; A least squares; DIAGNOSIS-A2 work/transient.py), the linear t = a + cycles / f, the median off by duration bin

reading.GONE: A(L) <= 8 us (R3's own 1410 sag is 6.1 us and sits in T0)
reading.REDUCED: A(L) <= 0.5 x A(1410) on this board's f1410 page (nodrop); if f1410 is still missing, A2's fit of the same page, 29.652628 us (tau 300 us; results/published/2026-10-21-nvidia_gh200_480gb-tileA2-session/results/2026-10-20-nvidia_gh200_480gb-olmoe-1b-7b-f128-r3-counters/lock1410/r3c-g64.json, another board)

constrains.F1: GONE at 1305: an apparatus fix exists at the ladder's own rung (time the wgmma tiles at 1305, F1 keeps only R3's baseline in T0); GONE at 1005 only: the fix needs 1005 (an owner decision on the timing lock); PRESENT at both: no apparatus escape, F1 is priced, and A(L), tau(L) are its per-lock constants (SEEN-MEASURED); REDUCED: F1 is priced with A(L) at the lock v5 times at

M2.decided_after: whether v5 and B2 time at 1005 MHz (should M2 read GONE only there) is decided by the owner after S1, with M2's numbers (owner, 2026-10-21); nothing here pre-commits it

M3.question: DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q7 row 3: does v4 over-predict Mixtral 128 G 1's w1 bytes (Q2's inference, about 7%)?
M3.cells: Mixtral 8x7B 128x128 G 1, n 2 PT, PW, uniform, balanced, NATIVE (docs/registered/2026-10-21-settleS1-hist/mixtral-8x7b-128g1-n.json)
M3.unit: weight sets per GEMM (q); e as a fraction
M3.quantity: q_counted = (dram__bytes_read.sum - n x the GEMM's A operand per tread) / the GEMM's weight set; e = q_pred / q_counted - 1 per key (v3, CLAMP) with q_pred registered below (byte_predictions_m3)

reading.W1-OVER: mean e(CLAMP, w1) over the 4 cells >= +4%

constrains.F3: W1-OVER: Q2's inference holds; F3's w1 re-read refit takes these rows (SEEN-FITTED) and is what moves Mixtral 128 G 1. W1-EXACT: bytes do not carry Mixtral 128 G 1's residual under F1 + F2 + F4 (+2.8 to +3.5%); F3 is not needed there and v5's knee and sag forms are re-examined on Mixtral. W1-PARTIAL: both

M4.question: DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q7 row 4: in the w2 (and w1) re-read excess at G 16 and 64 G 1, activation against weight re-reads
M4.cells: ladder (balanced) cells, arms NATIVE, SHARED and PRIVATE: Mixtral 128x128 G 16 treads 3, 4, 8; Mixtral 64x128 w8 G 1 tread 2 (the balanced cells of A2's b128g16 and b64g1 pages; R3 runs PRIVATE on its balanced ladder only, PRIVATE_SKEW_REFUSAL)
M4.instrument: A2's byte-page instrument at 1410, the ladder's treads by the S1 key byte-treads
M4.quantity: e_P = max(q_P - n, 0), PRIVATE's excess over its n weight sets (each M-tile its own copy: no weight slab is read twice, so the excess is re-read activations), at the K-call means and at PRIVATE's highest call (dram_counter_route.r3_weight_bracket, pinned); SHARED's re-read q_S - 1; a = min(e_P / (q_S - 1), 1), the largest share of SHARED's excess that can be activations

reading.B-DOMINATED: at every tread e_P <= 0.2 x (q_S - 1) or e_P <= 0.02 weight sets

constrains.F3: B-DOMINATED (w2): the w2 excess is weight re-reads; F3 refits M4's slab constants (C_B, beta_B, theta1, eps1_w2) per tile family and nothing else. A-DOMINATED: M4's charge-once A assumption fails at the wgmma tiles; F3 needs an activation re-read term, and the weight part of w2's over-prediction is larger than the byte pages show. MIXED: both terms; the reduced form (eps1, theta1 only) is not enough

M5.question: DIAGNOSIS-A2 Q7 row 5: the knee's mechanism (latency exposure at 2 CTAs per SM?)
M5.cells: 128x128 G 1 byte cells, NATIVE: Qwen2-57B n 1, 2 and OLMoE n 1, 2, 4, four labels each (docs/registered/2026-10-21-settleS1-hist/qwen2-57b-a14b-128g1-n.json, olmoe-1b-7b-128g1-n.json); x from about 0.3 to 1.15
M5.instrument: A2's byte-page instrument at 1410 plus three recorded metrics (scripts/dram_counter_route_s1.py --s1-stall-metrics): smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard_per_warp_active.pct, smsp__warp_issue_stalled_barrier_per_warp_active.pct, sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active
M5.unit: percent (per active warp for the stalls, of peak sustained active for the tensor pipe); x and y ratios
M5.quantity: per GEMM: the three metrics; floor_cyc = q (S c + F_g), q = ceil(live CTAs / 132), S = K / 64 (the tcommon.joint_cF form at the CAL-A constants below); bytes_cyc = counted reads / bw x lock; x_s1 = bytes_cyc / floor_cyc; y_s1 = cycles / max(floor_cyc, bytes_cyc); Spearman rho of x_s1 with each metric over the page's GEMM cells

reading.LATENCY: rho(x, long scoreboard) >= 0.6 and rho(x, tensor active) <= -0.6
reading.BARRIER: rho(x, barrier) >= 0.6 and rho(x, long scoreboard) < 0.6

constrains.F2: LATENCY: the soft knee is DRAM latency exposed at 2 CTAs per SM and 3 stages (Q5.2's INFERENCE supported); v5's knee exponent is a per-tile property tied to occupancy and stages, and 64x128 w8 (3 CTAs per SM) is expected between 128x128's 5.25 and R3's 14. BARRIER: the knee is pipeline synchronisation; its exponent is tied to num_stages. NONE-SEEN: F2 stays a SEEN-FITTED shape with no mechanism claimed

M5.source: c and F: A2's CAL-A floor calibration (A2's floor score, 'calibration'; SEEN); bw: v4's bandwidth, the CAL engine's v2 timing fit x[2] (rental 6's Pricer, regtile.pricer), as DIAGNOSIS-A2 knee.py's bytes_only term
